perplexed: Not sure what to think or do; mixed up.
roundabout: A short coat that fits close to the body. Boys wore it in the old days.
guile: Clever ways of making people believe something that is not true.
lick: To beat someone in a fight, or to hit as a way to teach a child. A 'lick' is a hit.
obleeged: A spoken form of a word that means you must do something.
whitewash: A cheap white mix of water and a white stuff. People put it on a wall to make it white.
taw: The big round glass ball that a player shoots at the other balls in the game.
morosely: In a sad way, with a bad feeling.
tallow: Hard fat from animals. People used it to make light and to keep things dry.
audacious: Showing no fear of what other people think; very brave and rude.
benediction: Words said at the end of a church meeting, asking God to be good to the people.
scarify: To make small cuts or lines on something. Here, Tom does this to a part of the house.
counterfeited: Made to look like the real thing, so that people think it is real. Here, it is about a copy of a Barlow.
disconcerted: Upset and mixed up because something went wrong.
cravat: A wide cloth that a man wears around his neck.
wily: Clever, in a way that is not honest.
sheepish: A little sorry and low, like a person who knows he did wrong.
tittering: Quiet laughing that you try to keep inside.
supplication: A serious request made in a low voice, especially to God.
prosy: Not interesting, because it is too long and says nothing new.
brimstone: A yellow stone that makes fire. In 'fire and brimstone' it means the fires of hell.
fillip: A quick push made with one part of the hand that is held back and then let go.
mortified: Said of a part of the body that is dead and going bad. Here, Tom says it about his foot.
expectorate: To send water from the mouth, in a rude way.
gaudy: With too many bright colors. Here, Tom likes Huck's wild life outside the rules.
hogshead: A very big round box for drink, made of wood.
spunk: In 'spunk-water', rain water in an old tree. The boys think it can take a small hard thing off the skin.
wart: A small, hard bit that grows on the skin.
ferule: A flat stick that a teacher used to hit a child on the hand.
gable: The part of an end wall of a house that goes up to a point at the top.
portentous: Looking very big and important, as if something bad may come.
tick: A very small animal that bites. The boys play with one.
grisly: Very bad to look at; it makes you afraid.
doublet: A short coat that fits close to the body, worn by men long ago.
cutlass: A short, heavy, curved sword used on ships long ago.
shingle: A thin flat piece of wood.
caitiff: An old word for a bad man who is weak and afraid.
lath: A thin, narrow piece of wood. The boys use laths as swords to play with.
doodlebug: A small animal that lives in a hole in the ground. The boys think it can answer questions.
ensconced: Sitting in a safe place where nobody can see.
caterwauling: The loud crying that cats make at night.
deathwatch: A small animal that makes a sound like a watch in wood. People thought it meant that someone would die.
pallid: Very white in the face, like a sick person.
tannery: A place where animal skins are worked on, to make them strong and fit to use.
verdigrease: A green stuff that grows on old metal and can make you ill.
escapade: An exciting thing to do that is against the rules.
phase: A spoken form of a word that means to trouble or upset someone.
electrified: Made to feel a sudden, strong surprise.
ostentatiously: In a way that is made to be seen by everyone.
palsy: An illness in which the body moves without control.
coroner: An officer who finds out how a person died. In the boys' game, the leader of a meeting for a dead cat, as a joke.
infatuated: Filled with a strong love for something that is not good for you.
inveterate: Always doing the same thing, for a long time, and not able to stop.
crestfallen: Sad because things did not go as you hoped.
smouldering: Giving off smoke, but with little or no fire.
sullied: Made less good; made to look bad.
freebooters: Men on ships who take things from others by force.
quicksilver: A shiny silver metal that is a liquid.
mutiny: When the people on a ship will not do what the leader says and fight against him.
quartering: Going across a river in a line that is not straight across but a little up the river.
ejaculations: Short, sudden cries or words said out loud.
weltering: Lying in something and rolling in it. Here, Tom is crying so much that he is all wet with it.
snifter: A small amount of strong drink or of smoke. It is said that one little bit would be too much for Johnny Miller.
charily: With care, because you are not sure.
inundation: Too much water that covers a place.
hendering: A country way of saying a word that means to keep someone from doing something.
spume: White bits on the top of water.
appalling: Very bad, so that it makes you afraid.
scalped: Cut the skin and hair from the head of an enemy, as some men did long ago.
soliloquized: Spoke out loud to herself when alone.
pregnant: Full of meaning. Here, it means full of signs of what will happen.
funereal: Sad and slow, like a time when a dead person is put in the ground.
transfixed: Not able to move, because of a big surprise.
rascalities: Bad acts that are not honest.
cowhide: A strong stick or rope made from the skin of an animal. It was used to hit people.
abashed: Feeling bad about yourself, and not knowing what to do.
slink: To go away quietly, because you feel bad about yourself.
artlessly: In a simple, honest way, with no plan.
humiliated: Feeling that other people see you as small or silly.
mercury: In 'a sudden falling of his mercury', a silver liquid in a glass that goes down when it gets cold. Here, Tom's good feeling goes down.
softy: A person who is too kind and weak.
dominie: A word for a teacher, used in Scotland.
gawky: Tall, and not good at moving.
declamatory: Like a loud speech that is made to sound big.
voluptuous: Full of nice feelings for the body and the senses.
gilded: Covered with gold, or with gold colour.
scuttle: A small hole with a cover, in the top of a room.
minstrel: In this story, a show with songs and jokes by men who act.
mesmerizer: A person who puts others in a state like sleep, to show something strange.
toils: Nets or ropes used to catch. Here, the law closes round Potter like a net.
diffident: Not sure of yourself, and so quiet.
hieroglyphics: Pictures and signs used as writing. The boys say the word in their own way.
sepulchral: Sounding deep and sad, like a voice from under the ground, where the dead are.
ha'nted: A spoken form of a word for a place where ghosts are.
switch: A thin stick that bends easily. It was used to hit a child when he did wrong.
hookey: Staying away from school when you should be there. 'Play hookey' means to do this.
knack: A natural way of doing something well and easily.
ambuscade: A secret attack from a place where nobody can see you. Here, Aunt Polly waits for Tom in the dark.
hollow: Empty, with no real meaning or good feeling inside.
skylarking: Playing around in a loud and silly way.
straitened: Small and not enough. Here, it is about Tom's little money and few things.
personating: Acting as if you are another person or thing.
covet: To want something very much, especially something that is another person's.
balmy: Warm and soft, in a nice way.
diluted: Made weaker by adding something. Here, she made the good words less strong.
sally: To go out quickly, as if to attack or help.
beseeching: Asking in a very serious way, because you need it so much.
galled: Made someone feel angry and hurt.
pew: A long seat in a church. It is made of wood.
preposterous: So silly and wrong that nobody can believe it.
seductive: Very nice to think of, so that you want to go to it. Here, the summer outside pulls Tom away from church.
simpering: Smiling in a silly way that is not real.
vagrant: A person who goes from place to place and has no home.
canvassed: Looked at, one part after another. Here, the boy looks at his body to find signs of sickness.
jubilant: Very happy because of a win.
deftly: In a quick and clever way, with good hands.
andiron: A metal stand that holds wood in a fire at home.
upbraid: To say angry words to a person about what he did wrong.
baffled: Not able to find the way. Here, people thought that going across water would stop someone from following.
nettle: A plant that hurts your skin when you touch it.
ingenuity: The power to think of clever ways to do things.
fuddled: Not able to think well, often because of drink.
ruffian: A rough man who likes to hurt people.
miscreant: A very bad person who does bad things.
quack: Not real and not honest. A 'quack' medicine is a bad medicine that does not work.
avariciously: With a very strong wish to get things for yourself.
numskull: A person who is not clever.
sweetmeat: A sweet food, like fruit with sugar on it.
true-blue: Always true to his friends and to what he believes.
lethargy: A heavy feeling that makes you want to rest and do nothing.
conned: Studied and thought about, so that you know it well.
flaying: A very hard beating. Here, it means the teacher's hard hitting of Tom.
retribution: Bad things that happen to a person because of the wrong he did.
mellow: Soft and easy; slow and happy. Here, it is because of drink.
unpalatable: Not nice to hear or to accept.
deposed: Told the court, as a promise, what he knows.
lynch: To kill a person by a crowd, with no court.
obliterated: Taken away completely, so that nothing can be seen.
unkempt: Not clean and not in order; with bad hair and clothes.
serape: A bright cloth from Mexico that men wear on the shoulders, like a big cover.
sombrero: A very wide Mexican cover for the head, with a high top.
milksop: A weak man who is afraid. It is not a nice word.
swag: Things that were taken from other people by a bad man.
gloating: Being glad in a bad way about something that you have or may get.
sachem: A chief of a Native American people. The man in the story uses it when he talks big.
debris: The broken pieces that are left when a thing is broken up.
nobby: Fine and in good style; very good.
attrition: The slow wearing down of something. Here, thinking about the events slowly makes them clear.
ostentatious: Made to be seen by people so that they will think well of it.
blindfold: To cover something so that no light comes out. Here, Tom puts a cloth over the light.
lair: A place where a wild animal or a bad man goes to be safe.
hispy: A children's game where some boys go away and one looks for them.
chartered: Paid for, so that you can use it for a special reason.
stile: Steps that let people go over a wall.
sumach: A tall plant with red fruit that grows on hills.
precarious: Not safe; it may fall at any time.
horsewhipped: Hit with a long thin stick, to hurt a person who did wrong.
vagabond: A person who goes from place to place and has no home.
posse: A group of men who are called to help catch a bad man.
embellishment: An extra thing added to a story, to make it better.
beholden: Having to say thank you to someone who helped you.
swooned: Went weak and fell down, not knowing anything.
stupor: A heavy state in which you cannot think or feel well.
powwow: A meeting with much talk. The word comes from Native American speech.
reverberations: Sounds that go on and on, coming back many times.
frescoed: Covered with writing or pictures on a wall. Here, names are on the walls, made with smoke.
sinuous: Going one way and then the other.
stalactite: A long stone shape that comes down from the top, in a big hole under the ground.
stalagmite: A stone shape that grows up from the floor, in a big hole under the ground.
clammy: Cold and wet, and not nice to touch.
sarcasm: Words that say the other thing from what you think, said to hurt or laugh at someone.
avocations: The jobs or work that people do every day.
petitioner: A person who asks for something in a serious way. Here, he asks God for help.
sheathed: Covered with a thin piece of metal.
ironically: In a way that says the other thing from what is true, often to make fun.
pardon: A paper that says a person is free and does not have to pay for what he did.
pallet: A simple bed on the floor, made from old covers or dry grass.
orgies: Parties with too much food, drink and noise. The boy does not know exactly what they are.
lucifer: In 'lucifer matches', the old name of matches that you light by pulling them across something rough.
waylay: To wait for people on the road and stop them, to take their things.
slope: A word that means to go away quickly and secretly.
blowout: A big, loud party with much food.
effusive: Showing happiness or thanks in a very strong way.
laudations: Words that say a person is good.
counterfeit: Made to look real when it is not. Here, the surprise of the people was not real.
magnanimous: Kind and good to someone who did wrong to you.
insipid: With no taste and no interest.
vittles: A country way to say 'food'. It comes from an older word.
ornery: A country word that means angry, mean or common.
